text:
arjun: heads up — saw a massive wakeup wave in us-west1 around 11:02 PT, ~480 concurrent cold-starts for gpu-nodepool. latency spiked to 3.2s on tokenization and 12s for first token.

maria: ugh. any idea what triggered it?

arjun: looks like a scheduled cron job plus a customer batch fan-out. lots of tiny requests hitting different model versions. time-series attached: https://grafana.redwood/prod/d/scale/gpu-wakeups?panel=7 (link)

sasha: can you paste the autoscaler events?

arjun: sure — snippet from cluster-autoscaler events:

```
I0409 11:02:01 cluster-autoscaler: Pod default/job-processor-xyz is pending due to InsufficientGPU
I0409 11:02:02 cluster-autoscaler: Scale-up: taking 40 nodes in nodepool-gpu-usw1
I0409 11:02:05 cluster-autoscaler: Added nodes: ip-10-0-1-xx
I0409 11:02:12 autoscaler: NodeReady event count spike
```

maria: devops-bot also posted heaps of `FailedScheduling` alerts earlier.

devops-bot: [alert] 1968001235 — 200 pods pending due to InsufficientGPU in us-west1-gpu-pool (:rotating_light:)

liam: sounds like a thundering herd during coldstart. we need smoothing: either client-side queueing or server-side admission control. token-bucket + allowlist for high-priority customers?

sasha: agree. also we should add jittered warm-pool wakeups and a leaky-bucket admission gate in front of the router to pace requests into the warm-pool. small prewarm of 10 nodes per AZ would mitigate 80% of these spikes.

arjun: thinking of two parallel fixes: 1) short-term: admission gate + small per-AZ reserve (10 nodes) with immediate prewarm; 2) medium-term: predictive warm-pool using recent qps derivative and scheduled cron detection.

maria: for short-term, what config changes? can we tune nodepool `autoscaling` and `scaleDown` params?

sasha: yes — example changes:

```
# nodepool config snippet
maxNodes: 200
minNodes: 0
reservedCapacity: 10  # per AZ hot reserve
scaleDownUnneededTime: 20m
scaleDownUnreadyTime: 30m
```

sasha: plus a router admission gate config: `max_wakeups_per_minute` and jitter window.

liam: proposal for router gate (simplified):

```
# pseudocode
token_bucket(capacity=50, refill_rate=10/s)
if token_bucket.try_consume(): allow_request()
else queue_request(timeout=3s) or return 429
```

maria: queueing with a short timeout is fine for non-streaming requests. streaming/chat requests should skip the queue and use high-priority path (and fail fast if no capacity).

arjun: can we implement token-bucket in the edge proxy quickly? I can ship a small PR to envoy filter or our edge lambda.

liam: envoy filter would be ideal. I'll sketch a filter with `x-redwood-priority` header support. If header high -> bypass queue up to reserved tokens.

oncall-bot: [notice] 1968001260 — created incident INC-2026: GPU wakeup surge — investig. assigned to arjun, sasha.

arjun: working on a dashboard to track wakeup ramp slope, warm-pool utilization, and queue latencies. rough query: `rate(prewarm_requests[1m])` and derivative of `qps` to detect > 50rps/s spike.

sasha: small experiments to run:
- enable reservedCapacity=10 in canary region (us-west1)
- deploy envoy token-bucket filter behind feature flag
- tune `scaleDownUnneededTime` from 10m -> 20m to reduce churn

maria: cost question — 10 nodes reserved across 3 AZs = 30 nodes. rough monthly delta?

sasha: ballpark: 30 p3-equivalent nodes ~ $50k/mo. but compare to lost SLA and egress of retries during spikes — often cheaper. we can make reserve autoscale down at night with schedule to reduce cost.

arjun: alternative: keep reserve as tiny warm-pool (low-power instance type) and migrate model load there for first N tokens then hop to GPU for heavy compute. that reduces pure-GPU reserve cost.

liam: nice idea — hybrid warm-pool. need to validate latency penalty for 0->gpu hop.

maria: timeline? can we do short-term changes this sprint?

arjun: I'll open two PRs today: envoy gate + update nodepool reserve canary. sasha can roll the canary. liam will draft token-bucket envoy config.

sasha: I'll monitor canary metrics and abort if tail latency worsens. planning rollout to us-west1 first. :eyes:

arjun: closing loop — follow-up in #eng-infra tomorrow with graphs. thanks all. :thumbsup:
